answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, skip the 22-miler. It would land on Sun Oct 4, 14 days before the race, and a run that long takes more than a week to recover from fully. That would eat into your taper for very little extra fitness.

You already have what you need. Your 20 on Sep 13 took 3:20 at an even pace, and last week's 17 came with no pain. For a 3:45 goal, the gains now come from practising race pace and arriving fresh, not from more distance.

Instead, Sun Oct 4 is an 18-miler with 6 miles at marathon pace. It gives you about 2 hours 50 minutes on your feet and your first rehearsal of goal pace on tired legs.

new.analysis:
The race move costs you two weeks of build, but the fitness you need is already in place. Weekly mileage has run between 40 and 53 for three weeks. Every session last week was done as planned, with 42.0 miles against 42.1 planned.

Your body is absorbing the work well. Easy runs held 9:52 per mile at heart rate 138, pain was 0/10 all week, and the Wednesday threshold reps faded only 1% at 7:58 per mile. Your easy share of 61% looks low, but that is expected with a threshold day and a long run whose heart rate drifts into zone 3 after the first hour.

This week holds volume flat at 42 miles but trims the threshold work to 4.5 miles instead of 6. Threshold fitness will not fade in two weeks, but tired legs would make Sunday's marathon-pace blocks sloppy. Marathon pace of 8:35 is about 35 seconds per mile slower than your threshold pace, so the two sessions train different things.

Nerves about the new date are normal, and the best response is to trust the taper. From Mon Oct 5, volume comes down while a little faster running stays in, so you arrive sharp rather than flat. The two weeks you lost would have added only a small gain compared with the freshness the taper gives you.
